pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, A Street in Jerusalem — a narrow lane of golden limestone running under a great pointed arch into the old city, latticed windows and a stone dome standing up in the sunlight above it, awnings and stalls crowding both sides, and the people of the town coming and going in the shadow below, an old man with a staff and a white headcloth walking out into the light with a boy and a dog ahead of him, there was a feast of the jews, and jesus went up to jerusalem, …

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Cripples — two beggars with their legs gone propped on short wooden crutches on a patch of green before a brick wall, one of them kneeling on leather-strapped pads with his back to us, both in white smocks pinned over with foxtails, the nearer one turning his open mouth up as if calling after the woman in a black cloak and wide hat who is walking away from them with an empty bowl held out behind her, a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed, …

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — a bald old man in a worn blue working suit sitting hunched forward on a yellow rush chair by the fire, his elbows driven down on his knees and both fists pressed hard against his eyes, his heavy boots planted on the bare boards and the whole room painted in the same restless blue strokes as the man himself, i have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred, …

pictures.scene: Melone, On the Road to Emmaus — two travellers walking barefoot along a track above a bay, the grey-bearded one in a blue tunic and a great orange cloak turning back with his hand lifted as he talks, the younger beside him in a green robe gathering a rose mantle over his arm, a walled hill town with towers standing above the road behind them and another hand reaching in at the edge of the picture toward the old man's shoulder, he picked up his mat and began to walk, …
pictures.name: pd_melone_wandelt

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Sabbath Rest — a poor green-walled room at rest, a young man in a dark cap holding an open book up to the light of a curtained window and reading half aloud, a woman in a rose shawl standing behind him with her eyes lowered, an old white-bearded man asleep in a chair with a child's head fallen on his arm, a woman wrapped in grey listening with her back to us, and a brass lamp hanging unlit from the ceiling, this is the sabbath, it is unlawful for you to carry your mat, …

pictures.scene: Liebermann, The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple — a boy in a plain pale shift standing on the stone floor of a dark temple hall with His back half turned to us, talking quietly to the teachers seated in front of Him, an old man in a white headcloth and a striped prayer shawl leaning forward to listen, another bearded elder bowed with his hand over his mouth, more men crowded at a reading desk on the left with an open book and leaning over the rail above, afterward, jesus found the man at the temple, …
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Millais, Christ in the House of His Parents — a carpenter's shop floored with wood shavings, a red-haired boy in a long pale smock standing barefoot by the bench and holding up His cut hand while His mother kneels in a deep blue gown and white headcloth to put her face against His, the carpenter leaning across the planks to take the hand and look at it, an old woman in an orange shawl watching from behind the bench, saws and a set square and a ladder hanging on the plank wall, to this very day my father is at his work, and i too am working, …

pictures.scene: Breu, The Crowd Cries Out Against Him — a press of accusers shouting up the pale stone steps of a judgment hall, a high priest in a jewelled mitre and a gold mantle counting off the charge on his fingers with his eyes lowered, an elder in a black cap and white fur collar leaning in under his hand with a rolled writ gripped in his fist and his mouth open, a bearded man in another jewelled cap staring from behind them and heads in red and green hoods packed above with their mouths open and their arms thrown up, the jews tried all the harder to kill him, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — a dying old man propped up in white linen on a bed spread with a great red coverlet, laying his open right hand on the fair head of the younger boy, his son in a pale turban and a brown robe leaning over him with one hand lifted to move the blessing across and the other holding the child steady, the darker-haired boy watching from beside the bed and their mother standing in deep red at the right, the father loves the son and shows him all he does, …

pictures.scene: Vermeer, Woman Holding a Balance — a woman in a blue fur-lined jacket and a white linen headcloth standing at a table in a still room, holding an empty balance up between her fingers and watching it settle, strings of pearls and gold chains spilled out of an open box onto the blue cloth at her elbow, the light coming in from a shuttered window at the left, and a dark painting of the Last Judgment hanging on the wall just behind her head, the father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the son, …
pictures.name: pd_vermeer_balance

pictures.scene: Bocklin, The Isle of the Dead — a small rowing boat crossing still black water toward an island of tawny rock, a tall grove of black cypresses standing up out of the middle of it against a cold grey evening sky, square tomb doors cut into the cliffs on either side, a boatman bent over the oars, and one figure standing upright in the bow wrapped head to foot in white beside a white-draped bier, he has crossed over from death to life, …

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ sitting in a pale blue robe inside a deep blue almond of light ringed all round with small cherub heads, His right hand lifted in judgment and His left hand open, gold rays spreading out behind Him over the whole gold ground, His mother kneeling at the left with her hands joined and crowned saints and angels standing in ranks on both sides, and one winged angel below holding up the cross, he has given him authority to execute judgment, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Bouguereau, The Holy Women at the Tomb — three women in dark mourning cloaks come at dawn to a grey stone tomb and stopped dead in the doorway of it, one kneeling with her hands clasped under her chin and her face turned up, another standing barefoot behind her with her hand against her brow, the third sunk on her knees at the right with a great brass dish of spices sliding out of her arm, and inside the opened grave a white angel standing in the light with one arm raised, all who are in their graves will hear his voice, …
pictures.name: pd_bouguereau_de_heilige_vrouwen_bij_het_graf

pictures.scene: Delaroche, Joan of Arc Questioned in Prison — an old cardinal in a scarlet gown and cap sitting forward on a stool in a dark cell with a gold cross on his breast and one hand spread on his knee, turning his head to question the girl beside him, a clerk behind his shoulder writing it down, and the prisoner sitting up on a heap of straw in a plain white shift with an iron chain on her wrists and her hands folded together, looking past him with her eyes lifted, i judge only as i hear, and my judgment is just, …
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a preacher in a rough brown coat standing bare-headed under the trees of a wood with both hands open as he speaks, hundreds of country people packed round him on the slope in hoods and white kerchiefs and broad straw hats, a quiet figure in pale blue standing apart among them at the right, boys climbed up into the branches above to see over the heads, and a woman with a baby and a man with a staff sitting with their backs to us in the near foreground, you have sent to john, and he has testified to the truth, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ standing barefoot at night in a pale robe and a heavy jewelled clasp with a dark red mantle over His shoulder, a crown of thorns and a thin gold halo about His head, carrying a pierced horn lantern low in His left hand so that its candlelight throws up over His face and the weeds, His right hand raised to knock at a long-shut door that is grown over with ivy and dead nettles and has no handle on His side, john was a lamp that burned and gave light, …
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Van Eyck, God the Father Enthroned — an enthroned figure seen close and straight on, bearded, with long dark hair falling either side of a calm face, wearing a high jewelled triple crown set with pearls and sapphires over a deep red mantle, a broad gold morse of pearls and blue stones clasping it at the breast, one hand lifted in blessing at the edge of the picture, and behind the head a halo of thin gold rays inside a gold arch lettered in Latin, you have never heard his voice nor seen his form, …
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_god_the_father

pictures.scene: Spitzweg, The Bookworm — a white-haired old scholar standing high on the top step of a library ladder in a black coat and breeches, holding one open volume up close to his nose in the shaft of light, a second book open in his lower hand, a third gripped under his arm and a fourth squeezed between his knees, shelves of books running up out of sight on every side of him and a carved sign over the case beside his head, you pore over the scriptures, …
pictures.name: pd_spitzweg_boekenwurm

lines.text: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.
One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, Do you want to get well?
Sir, the invalid replied, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.
Then Jesus told him, Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.
Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk. Now this happened on the Sabbath day,
so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.
But he answered, The man who made me well told me, Pick up your mat and walk.
Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk? they asked.
But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.
Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.
And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.
But Jesus answered them, To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.
Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
So Jesus replied, Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.
The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.
Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,
so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.
And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice
and come out, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.
There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.
You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.
John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.
But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish, the very works I am doing, testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.
And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,
nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent.
You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,
yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.
I do not accept glory from men,
but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.
I have come in My Father's name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.
How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?
